Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

rear noun

the back part; at the rear

also at the rear, in the rear, the rear of, rear (adjective), back (the back part), bring up the rear

classical

Cic. Phil. 3.32: ā tergō, ā fronte, ā lateribus tenēbitur (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 202: ā tergō (+ gen.)

ā tergō

from behind, at the rear

From the back, behind: the usual way of saying where something is or comes from at the rear. Traupman gives it with the genitive for “in the rear of”.

Other words

  • pars posterior — the back part

    also used · classical

    The rear of a house, a cart or an animal: posterior pars domūs. The adjective posterior answers to “rear” (see back-seat, sēdēs posterior).

  • novissimum agmen — the rear (of a column on the march)

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.15 (Lewis & Short, s.v. novus)

    Of an army or any file of people; novissimī are those at the back. To bring up the rear is agmen claudere (Caes. BG 1.25, Lewis & Short s.v. claudō).

Examples

  • Pater agmen claudit; nōs praecēdimus.

    Dad brings up the rear; we go on ahead.composed

See also back, behind, back seat, back door.

SourcesLewis & Short: tergum · Lewis & Short: posterior · Lewis & Short: novus · Lewis & Short: claudo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 202, checked against the searchable text of the book.
